newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Hospital says not relying on insurance.
newsitem.headline: Australian Hospital says not relying on insurance.

text.p: Private hospital operator Australian Hospital Care Ltd said on Thursday a successful private health care business did not necessarily depend on a buoyant health insurance sector.

"The Australian population has certain lifestyles and expectations that can be better accommodated by the private health care sector, and at our listing we made a point of the fact that our occupancy levels had increased over the year despite a fall in health insurance," chief executive officer Mark Bryce told a Securities Institute of Australia briefing.
"We can continue to grow and successfully grow despite declining health insurance," he said.
He cited opportunities for revenue diversification in contracting to governments and allied medical care.

Foreign competition was not yet a major threat in the industry, and although Bryce said the presence of foreign interests would help contestability in privatisations he was comfortable with his firm's ability to capitalise on opportunities.
"The question is are there enough players in the market in the private sector to be able to cope with the privatisation opportunities," Bryce told Reuters after the briefing.
"We are very comfortable with our capacity to be able to meet the opportunities," he said.
Bryce confirmed that Australian Hospital Care, which listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in August 1996, was on track to meet its full year prospectus forecasts.
In April the company reported a net profit for the six months to December 31 of A$6.8 million, struck on revenue of A$94.6 million.
Australian Hospital Care shares ended four cents higher at A$2.37 on turnover of 80,008 shares.
